note: Honest, sourced catalog. kind=action (FrameForge applies+reverts it), verify (read-only health check, never an 'action'), advise (BIOS/manual/in-game — we guide, we don't fake it). Every action records prior state before changing so revert is exact.

tweaks.name: Disable Game DVR background recording
tweaks.summary: Turns off the Xbox Game Bar background recorder.
tweaks.details: Game DVR continuously buffers gameplay so you can 'record that'. That capture costs GPU encoder time and CPU and is one of the most reliably measurable FPS/stutter wins when turned off.
tweaks.evidence: Reproduced in many before/after captures; the background DVR thread competes for the GPU encoder.

tweaks.name: Windows Game Mode
tweaks.summary: Ensures Game Mode is on so Windows defers background work while you play.
tweaks.details: Game Mode suppresses background interruptions (driver installs, defrag, Update installs) during a game, reducing stutter from background CPU spikes. Low but free.
tweaks.evidence: Microsoft-documented behavior prioritizing the active game.

tweaks.name: Performance power plan (no min-state pin)
tweaks.summary: Activates Ultimate Performance but explicitly UN-pins minimum processor state.
tweaks.details: Removes CPU core parking and idle-demotion latency for steadier frametimes. Crucially, FrameForge sets minimum processor state to 5% (NOT 100%) — on a 13th/14th-gen Intel chip, pinning min state at 100% keeps cores out of low-power states and raises the idle voltage floor, the exact condition linked to Raptor Lake Vmin-shift aging. This gives the latency benefit without the aging risk.
tweaks.evidence: Intel guidance against sustained elevated voltage on Raptor Lake; power-plan core-parking removal reduces scheduling latency.

tweaks.name: Disable Windows Update P2P (Delivery Optimization)
tweaks.summary: Stops Windows from uploading/downloading updates peer-to-peer in the background.
tweaks.details: Delivery Optimization can use your bandwidth and CPU to seed Windows/Store updates to other PCs while you game, causing latency spikes and bandwidth contention. Setting download mode to HTTP-only (no peering) keeps updates working but ends the background P2P.
tweaks.evidence: Documented DODownloadMode policy; mode 0 disables peering.

tweaks.name: Trim desktop animations (cosmetic)
tweaks.summary: Disables window/taskbar animations for a snappier desktop and overlays.
tweaks.details: Cosmetic: negligible effect on fullscreen in-game FPS, but reduces compositor work so Alt-Tab and overlays feel instant. Tagged honestly as low/cosmetic.
tweaks.evidence: DWM animation cost; perceptual snappiness, not FPS.

tweaks.name: Disable mouse acceleration (Enhance Pointer Precision)
tweaks.summary: Turns off Windows pointer acceleration for 1:1, consistent aim.
tweaks.details: Enhance Pointer Precision speeds the cursor up the faster you move, so the same physical motion maps to different in-game angles. Competitive players disable it for muscle-memory consistency. This affects aim consistency / input feel, not FPS. Fully reversible.
tweaks.evidence: Raw, acceleration-free input is the standard competitive configuration; 1:1 mapping is reproducible.

tweaks.name: Disable USB selective suspend
tweaks.summary: Stops Windows from power-gating USB devices (mouse/keyboard/controller).
tweaks.details: USB selective suspend lets Windows put idle USB devices to sleep to save power. On a gaming desktop this can cause brief input-device hitches or micro-disconnects. Disabling it keeps your peripherals always-on. Reversible — FrameForge records and restores the prior AC/DC values.
tweaks.evidence: Selective suspend power-gates idle USB endpoints; disabling removes wake latency for input devices.

tweaks.name: Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling
tweaks.summary: Should be ON — required for NVIDIA Reflex and DLSS Frame Generation latency paths.
tweaks.details: HAGS lets the GPU manage its own frame queue, reducing CPU overhead and enabling the lowest-latency Reflex/Frame-Gen paths on RTX 40/50-series. We verify it's on rather than toggling it (toggling needs a reboot).
tweaks.evidence: NVIDIA requires HAGS for the Reflex/Frame-Generation low-latency pipeline.

tweaks.name: Raptor Lake microcode (Vmin-shift mitigation)
tweaks.summary: Confirms your 14900KF is on the patched microcode that mitigates the 13th/14th-gen instability.
tweaks.details: Intel's 0x12B microcode (and BIOS updates) address the Vmin-shift degradation that affected some 13th/14th-gen K chips. This is a stability/longevity check, not an FPS toggle — but a degrading chip silently loses performance and crashes. If your microcode is older, update the BIOS.

tweaks.name: Receive Side Scaling (NIC)
tweaks.summary: Should be ON so network interrupts spread across CPU cores.
tweaks.details: RSS distributes NIC interrupt processing across multiple cores instead of pinning core 0. Default-on; we verify it rather than 'fixing' something that isn't broken.
tweaks.evidence: Documented RSS behavior; default-enabled on modern adapters.

tweaks.name: Intel Default Settings power profile (BIOS — do FIRST)
tweaks.summary: Apply the Intel-recommended power guardrail (PL1/PL2/ICCMax) in BIOS before any memory OC.
tweaks.details: MSI's default 'unlimited' power can push the 14900KF past Intel's spec, contributing to instability/aging. Set the Intel Default Settings (Performance: PL1/PL2 = 253W, ICCMax = 307A) in BIOS first. This protects the chip and is the recommended ordering BEFORE enabling XMP.
tweaks.evidence: Intel Default Settings guidance for Raptor Lake stability (2024).
guide: Reboot and press Del to enter the MSI BIOS
Go to OC → CPU Cooler Tuning (or 'Intel Default Settings')
Choose 'Intel Default Settings' → 'Performance' (PL1/PL2 253W, ICCMax 307A)
Save & Exit (F10)

tweaks.name: Enable XMP — DDR5 5600 (BIOS — do AFTER Intel Default Settings)
tweaks.summary: Your RAM runs 4800 but is rated 5600 — enabling XMP is the single biggest free CPU-bound FPS lever here.
tweaks.details: Memory bandwidth/latency is one of the largest CPU-bound FPS levers on Raptor Lake. Detected DDR5 rated 5600 running at 4800 (XMP off). Enabling XMP Profile 1 typically yields high-single-digit to mid-teens % gains in CPU-bound titles. Do this AFTER setting Intel Default Settings so the platform is stable first. BIOS-only — Windows cannot toggle it.
tweaks.evidence: Outlet 1080p CPU-bound benchmarks: DDR5-4800 → rated XMP delivers large avg and 1%-low uplifts on 13th/14th gen.
guide: Reboot and press Del to enter the MSI BIOS
In EZ Mode, find the XMP/EXPO switch (top of screen) — or OC → Extreme Memory Profile (XMP)
Select Profile 1 (DDR5-5600)
Save & Exit (F10). If it fails to POST, clear CMOS and try Memory Try It at 5600.

tweaks.name: Resizable BAR (BIOS)
tweaks.summary: Let the CPU access all 16GB of VRAM at once — verify it's enabled.
tweaks.details: Resizable BAR can improve performance in some titles by removing the 256MB VRAM aperture limit. On Z790 + RTX 5080 it should be on. Verify in the NVIDIA App (System → Resizable BAR) or BIOS (Re-Size BAR Support = Enabled, requires Above 4G Decoding).
guide: Open the NVIDIA App → System → check 'Resizable BAR'
If Off: reboot → Del → BIOS → Settings → Advanced → PCIe → enable 'Above 4G Decoding' and 'Re-Size BAR Support'
Save & Exit

tweaks.name: Enable NVIDIA Reflex in-game
tweaks.summary: The real latency win — turn Reflex On/On+Boost in each game that supports it.
tweaks.details: NVIDIA Reflex reduces render-queue latency far more effectively than any driver/registry tweak, often 20–40ms. Prefer the in-game Reflex toggle over the driver's Low Latency Mode. Pair with HAGS on and a frame cap below your refresh.
tweaks.evidence: NVIDIA Reflex measured click-to-photon latency reductions across supported titles.
guide: In each supported game's Video/Graphics settings, find 'NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency'
Set it to 'On' (or 'On + Boost' for the lowest latency)
Keep HAGS enabled and cap FPS just below your refresh for the best latency

tweaks.name: Use wired 2.5G Ethernet, not Wi-Fi
tweaks.summary: For online games, a wired connection slashes latency variance vs Wi-Fi.
tweaks.details: Wi-Fi adds jitter and packet loss that no registry tweak can fix. Your board has Intel 2.5G Ethernet — use it for competitive play. This affects ping/consistency, not raw FPS.
tweaks.evidence: Wired vs Wi-Fi latency-jitter is well established.
guide: Plug an Ethernet cable into the board's 2.5G port
Windows will prefer it automatically when connected

tweaks.name: Move active games + shader cache to the 980 PRO
tweaks.summary: Keep the games you actually play on the fast NVMe, not the slower QLC SATA SSD.
tweaks.details: The Samsung 860 QVO is QLC SATA — fine for storage, but slower for texture streaming and shader compilation, which can show up as traversal stutter and longer shader-comp hitches. Keep your active library and the DirectX shader cache on the 980 PRO (NVMe).
tweaks.evidence: QLC SATA sustained-write/random-read deficits vs NVMe TLC affect streaming/shader-comp stutter.
guide: In Steam: Settings → Storage → add/select the 980 PRO drive → move your active games there
Windows: Settings → System → Display → Graphics → leave shader cache default (driver caches to the OS drive — keep the OS on the 980 PRO)

tweaks.name: Disable Nagle's algorithm (TCP games only)
tweaks.summary: Advise-only: helps a few TCP-based games, useless for UDP shooters (CS2/Valorant/Apex).
tweaks.details: Nagle batches small TCP packets, adding a few ms. Disabling can help latency in TCP-based online games, but most competitive shooters use UDP where this does nothing. Because it requires fragile per-interface GUID matching and a reboot, FrameForge advises rather than auto-applies it.
tweaks.evidence: Nagle batching delay applies only to TCP; UDP titles unaffected.
guide: Only do this for TCP-based games
Under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces\{your-active-GUID}, add DWORD TcpAckFrequency=1 and TCPNoDelay=1
Reboot. Remove both values to revert.
